answer: Sequential proof-of-work chains resist Sybil attacks: each identity must carry a chain of work proofs where every proof builds on the previous one, like strata in rock. A veteran owns a deep relic of months of verified work; a fresh fake starts at zero depth and cannot buy history. Each proof takes real compute time and must reference the one before it, so a marble-smooth forgery still lacks the chain. Timing with quartz precision exposes bursts: a thousand identities minted in one hour share identical timing and get flagged. The attacker pays sequential cost per fake, with no bulk discount.
